questions.question: Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows(s) from the statements Statements: All goats are black some black are white. No black is gold. Conclusions: I. Some goats are white II. Some goats being gold is a possibility.

some black are white.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some goats are white - False (Because, No definite relation given between goats and white, so it can be possible only).

II. Some goats being gold is a possibility - False (Because, All goats are black and no black is gold, so no goats will be gold).

Statements: Some keys are scales All books are papers. All scales are papers. Conclusions: (i) No books are keys. (ii) Some papers are keys.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some keys are scales

All books are papers.

All scales are papers.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

Conclusions:

I. No books are keys - False (Because, No definite relation given between books and keys, so it can be possible only).

II. Some papers are keys - True (Because, Some keys are scales and All books are papers, so those part of keys which is scales will also papers).

So, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.solution:

questions.question: Direction: In the question below are given three statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts. Statement: All Teachers are Master. Only a few Parents are Principal. Some Master are Parents. Conclusion: I) Some Principals are Teacher. II) Some Parents are not Principal.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In the question below are given three statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Statement:

All Teachers are Master.

Only a few Parents are Principal.

Some Master are Parents.

Conclusion:

I) Some Principals are Teacher.

II) Some Parents are not Principal.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is shown below according to the given information.

Statement:

All Teachers are Master.

Only a few Parents are Principal.

Some Master are Parents

Conclusion:

I) Some Principals are Teacher → Does not follow → As all Teachers are Master or Only a few Parents are Principal and Some Master are Parents. So Some Principal are Teacher is not definitely followed.

II) Some Parents are not Principal → Follow → As Only a few Parents are Principal. So, Some Parents are not Principal is definitely followed.

So, Only Conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

Important Points

1) "Only a few" means is the combination of "Some" and "Some not".

2) Example:- Only a few A are B means Some A are B and Some A are not B.

3) Only a few A are B means only a specific part of A is B and the remaining part of the A is not B.

questions.question: In this question, three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Choose the conclusion(s) which best fit(s) logically. Statements: 1) Some actors are writers. 2) All writers are dancers. 3) No actor is a director. Conclusions: I. No writer is an actor. II. Some actors are dancers. III. Some writers are not directors.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Choose the conclusion(s) which best fit(s) logically.

Statements:

1) Some actors are writers.

2) All writers are dancers.

3) No actor is a director.

Conclusions:

I. No writer is an actor.

II. Some actors are dancers.

III. Some writers are not directors.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
Concept:

1) We have to check the conclusions are 100% match with the statement. If the conclusion is 100% match with the given statement then the conclusion is true. If there is a 1% chance of not following the statement then the conclusion is considered to be false.

2) The possibility case can be considered to be "false" in "definite case".

3) In Possibility case, either "can" or "possible" word must be present.

The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

I. No writer is an actor. → False (As, Some actors are writers → so the conclusion cannot be true)

II. Some actors are dancers. → True (As, Some actors are writers and All writers are dancers → so some actors are dancers)

III. Some writers are not directors. → True (As, Some actors are writers, All writers are dancers, and No actor is a director → so some writers who are actors are not directors)

Hence, only conclusions II and III follow.

Additional Information
